It uses 10,000 simulated lineups to estimate how often two players appear together, enabling identification of high-leverage stacks. The model assumes that conditional co-ownership reflects real-world lineup behavior, which is validated through empirical data from 175-snap PBP simulations. Failure modes include overfitting to small sample sizes or misalignment between simulated and actual field behavior. The pay-up defense leverage primitive operates under the assumption that low-ownership defenses offer superior risk-adjusted returns. This is modeled as an inverse relationship between ownership and expected value, with a threshold beyond which leverage erodes. Wind sensitivity analysis applies a quantile shift model to adjust projections based on environmental factors. The model assumes that wind impacts vary predictably with velocity and position, and its breakdown occurs when wind exceeds 10 mph, causing disproportionate drops in projected yardage ceilings. These primitives form a coherent system for optimizing DFS portfolios under uncertainty.
